$comment: Per-profile access control. Point TERMIX_POLICY_FILE at a copy of this.
A profile is selected by the bearer token on the HTTP transport, or by
TERMIX_PROFILE on stdio.
EACH DIMENSION HAS A MODE, so you decide the scope of every restriction:
allowlist  default deny; permits what `allow` matches (deny carves
exceptions out of the grant).  Fails closed.
blocklist  default allow; refuses what `deny` matches (allow carves
exceptions back in).  Fails open.
all        no restriction on this dimension.
none       nothing passes.
Omit the mode and it is inferred: allowlist if you wrote `allow`, blocklist
if you wrote only `deny`, otherwise the default (hosts allowlist; tools and
paths all). Shorthand: "hosts": "all", or "hosts": ["a","b"] for an
allowlist of those.
globalBlocklist decides whether the server-wide TERMIX_BLOCKLIST still
applies to this profile: "enforce" (default) or "ignore".
Tool groups save enumerating names: @readonly @hosts @files @files.read
@files.write @exec @docker @system @tunnels @snippets @observability @meta
@policy @escape.  Run `node scripts/policy.mjs groups` to list members.
Check a policy before trusting it:
node scripts/policy.mjs validate ./access-policy.json
node scripts/policy.mjs explain  ./access-policy.json --profile ops
or, from a model, the access_policy_schema and access_policy_check tools.
Secrets: prefer tokenEnv / termixApiKeyEnv (or tokenSha256) so this file
carries no secret and can live beside the rest of your compose config.

readonly.description: Look at anything reachable, change nothing. The safe default.

ops.description: Day-to-day operations on the Docker and reverse-proxy hosts.
ops.$comment: Hosts as an allowlist: a machine added to Termix later is unreachable until granted here.
ops.$comment2: Tools as a blocklist: everything except the sharp edges.

appdata.description: Edit application config on one host, and nothing else.
$comment: @escape is denied on purpose. Path rules bind the file tools, but a
shell command reads and writes anywhere the SSH user can -- so a
path-restricted profile that keeps run_command is not path-restricted.
The server warns at startup if you leave these granted.

break-glass.description: Everything, including hosts the global blocklist excludes. Use deliberately.

audit.description: Read the audit trail and alerts only; cannot reach a machine at all.
